value.title: Alphabet-free uniform continuity of binary receiver curves
value.summary: A common-mixture coupling of the joint input-output laws at two binary input priors bounds both the input entropy change and the conditional input entropy change by h_2(|p-p'|). Subtraction yields |J_A(p)-J_A(p')|≤2h_2(|p-p'|), uniformly over the receiver output alphabet and also for generalized posterior-measure receivers.

value.title: Compact generalized receiver curves and uniform finite-output density
value.summary: Mean-one-half Borel posterior measures form a weakly compact space. Pointwise continuity of the posterior information integrand, together with the common binary-prior continuity modulus, upgrades weak convergence to uniform convergence of receiver curves. Carathéodory matching on any N-point grid containing 0, 1/2, and 1, followed by the common modulus, gives an at-most-N-output exact grid match with sup-norm error at most min{1,4h_2(Delta_Q)}. Reflection of the reduced measure preserves an already reflected pair on reflection-closed grids.

value.title: Exact 30-row receiver-curve sensitivity audit
value.summary: Combining identical signed receiver-information atoms in each accepted specialized row and applying the exact term sensitivities produces the audited rowwise coefficient pairs (a_r,b_r). Every pair is coordinatewise at most (4,4), so sup-norm receiver-curve perturbations epsilon_G and epsilon_K alter each row right side by at most a_r epsilon_G+b_r epsilon_K and universally by at most 4epsilon_G+4epsilon_K.

value.title: Relaxed-row stability and strict-feasibility persistence
value.summary: For a fixed auxiliary hierarchy, replacing G and K by uniformly close receiver curves preserves feasibility after relaxing row r by a_r epsilon_G+b_r epsilon_K; the reverse comparison follows by exchanging the receiver pairs. If every original row has slack exceeding its corresponding perturbation allowance, the same rates and hierarchy remain feasible, so strictly feasible witnesses persist under sufficiently fine finite-output approximations. The argument does not establish convergence of the unrelaxed optimized functional when rate-free constraints are active with zero margin.

value.title: Deterministic receiver-curve stability verifier
value.summary: A dependency-free standard-library checker validates the two declared dependency transactions, independently rebuilds the accepted generic length-three 30-row system, combines identical signed atoms, checks every audited (a_r,b_r) coefficient and the global (4,4) bound, and verifies the support, reflection, and mesh formulas for the explicit uniform grids. It does not mechanically prove the entropy-continuity, Carathéodory, or compactness arguments.

value.title: Uniform receiver-curve continuum bridge and 30-row stability
value.summary: Every binary-input receiver curve satisfies |J_A(p)-J_A(p')|≤2h_2(|p-p'|). Generalized mean-one-half posterior-measure receiver curves form a compact subset of C([0,1]) with uniformly dense finite-output curves; on every N-point grid Q containing 0, 1/2, and 1, an at-most-N-output exact grid match has sup-norm error at most min{1,4h_2(Delta_Q)}, while reflection-closed grids preserve an already reflected pair. For the accepted 30-row system, receiver errors epsilon_G and epsilon_K require only the audited row relaxations a_r epsilon_G+b_r epsilon_K, bounded universally by 4epsilon_G+4epsilon_K, and strictly feasible witnesses persist under sufficiently fine approximation. No unrelaxed optimized-value convergence, full-functional cardinality bound, reflected optimality, minimax interchange, numerical capacity improvement, or exact sum-capacity conclusion follows.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted continuum approximation and row-stability bridge directly advances the existing non-root objective of simplifying and optimizing the premise-bounded Theorem 9 auxiliary-receiver converse, specifically its active receiver-reduction thread.
